structure: Missouri 6-12 Grade-Level Expectations (Spring 2016) as a Word document made of 35 tables. Title block (u1-u4: heading, DESE, Spring 2016, nondiscrimination). Six numbered strands appear as table title cells: 1 History: Continuity and Change; 2 Government Systems and Principles; 3 Geographic Study; 4 Economic Concepts; 5 People, Groups and Cultures. Every table has a header row of six course columns: '6-8 American History | 9-12 American History | 6-8 World History | 9-12 World History | 6-8 Geography | 9-12 Government' (there is no 9-12 Geography and no 6-8 Government course column). So the grade band + course come from the column header (course = American History / World History / Geography / Government; grades = 6-8 or 9-12). Rows are 'Theme 1'..'Theme 6' (Theme 1 = tools of social science inquiry, Themes 2-6 = chronological periods/units whose cell text begins with a unit name, e.g. 'Settlements A.', 'Re-Emerging America A.', 'Structure of Government A.'), followed by lettered standards (A., B., C., ...) in the same cell. Each standard occupies two table rows (first column 'Theme N', then a duplicate row with first column 'Tools of Social Science Inquiry' for Theme 1 or 'Key concepts and Understandings' for Themes 2-6) with identical text; both are standards. Column index of a content cell equals the index of its header cell in the closest header row above (positions vary between tables, e.g. C2,C4,...C12 in tables 4, C3..C9 in table 32). First-column cells (strand title, Theme N, concept label) apply to all of 6-12 with course null. No standard codes in the text and no examples, glossary or resources in this file; the entire document after the title block is the standards grid.
